chunks: And Ribʿī narrated from al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Regarding a man to whom a bequest/executorship is entrusted,
He said: “If it is sent to him from another town, then he has no right to refuse it. But if he is in a city in which someone else besides him is found, then that is up to him.”

key_terms.فَذَاكَ إِلَيْهِ: the decision is left to him
key_terms.فِي مِصْرٍ: in a city or settled place
key_terms.يُوصَى إِلَيْهِ: a person appointed over a bequest or executorship

ai.seo_question: When may a person refuse being appointed to carry out a bequest in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about accepting an appointment as an executor of a bequest. If the appointment comes from another town, the person may not refuse it; but if he is in a city where others can serve in his place, the matter is left to his choice.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5446 - Ribʿi narrated from Al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasar from Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as)
regarding a man who is appointed as an executor.

Imam (as) said: "If the will is sent to him from another town, he does not have the right to reject it. However, if he is in a city where others are available, then it is up to him to accept or decline it."
